metadata.title: Exit times in non-Markovian drifting continuous-time random walk processes

extraction_notes.note: The paper has no theorem environments; its results are numbered equations introduced by prose ('it can be proven that', 'we find'). Each such sentence was made a claim node containing its numbered equation(s), and the preceding scenario argument a prose proof.

Classical renewal-theory and CTRW-propagator formulas restated without a name: TP1/TP2 are typed theorem (external) as cited/'well known' results stated in full, ClP20 kept a claim since it is presented as a derivation step of the example.

DP4 is one sentence introducing three symbols ($\mathbf{t}_b^{x,r}$, $T_b(x,r)$, $\mathbb{T}_b(x)$) and AssumP1 one sentence with three assumptions; a node cannot split a sentence, so each is kept as one node.

Worked cases with exponential/Erlang/stable distributions are long multi-paragraph examples; each was taken as one example node spanning all its numbered equations, with key claims nested inside ExP4.

Motivation, applications survey, Conclusions section, figure captions and the unnumbered inverse-Laplace eqnarray in Section 4 (kept inside ExP2) give no separate nodes; the $\varrho$ symbol is introduced inside the PP2 argument and has no definition node.
